patients.summary: Graphic designer in Chicopee who joins in 2021 with migraine, acne and a hydrochlorothiazide prescription from her prior practice. Asthma and seasonal rhinitis in 2022, OCD then GAD on sertraline, HCTZ photosensitivity in 2024, SLE presenting as class IV lupus nephritis in 2025 with complete renal response by mid-2026, and a serotonin syndrome ED visit in March 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — ESTABLISH CARE

29 y/o woman transferring primary care to us after years at another office. No acute concerns today; mainly wants a doctor she can reach.

Current issues she brings:
- Migraine without aura. Long-standing. Typical attacks a few times a month at most; sumatriptan 50 mg at onset takes care of nearly all of them, rarely needs the second dose. No change in pattern, no neuro symptoms with them.
- Acne vulgaris since her teens. Not on any prescription treatment, not much bothering her right now.
- Takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, prescribed by her previous PCP. Tolerating it.

No breathing, nasal or sinus complaints. Mood good, no anxiety concerns raised. PHQ-9 = 2.

MEDS (bottles reviewed): sumatriptan 50 mg PRN (max 200 mg/day); hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
ALLERGIES: NKDA.
PMH: as above. PSH: none.
FH: mother with SLE. Father with asthma and seasonal allergies. Sister with major depressive disorder.
SH: Graphic designer, schedule is flexible. Lives in Chicopee. Never smoker. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month. No recreational or illicit drug use.
GYN: last cervical cytology at her prior office in 2020, told it was normal; will confirm from records.
VACCINES: COVID Pfizer x2 (4/9 and 4/30/2021, card reviewed). No Tdap she can recall in the last 10 years.

EXAM
BP 101/64, HR 83, RR 15, T 36.9, SpO2 98% RA. Wt 65.4 kg, Ht 166.2 cm, BMI 23.7.
Well appearing. HEENT: normal, nasal passages clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or nodes. Lungs clear throughout. Heart: RRR, S1 S2 normal, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities: no edema. Skin: a few scattered comedones and small papules on the forehead and chin, no scarring. Neuro: grossly nonfocal. Mood and affect normal.

A/P
1. Establishing care. Records release signed. Baseline CBC and CMP today.
2. Migraine without aura — well controlled with as-needed sumatriptan. Refill when due.
3. Acne vulgaris — mild, no treatment wanted now. Revisit if it flares.
4. HCTZ 25 mg daily — continue, refills through us.
5. Prevention: one-time HIV and hepatitis C screening drawn today. Tdap given today. COVID series complete. Flu shot in the fall. Cervical screening next due 2023 if the 2020 result is confirmed normal.
6. Yearly physicals here going forward; message any time.

Seen with MA for rooming and vaccine.

documents.title: Breathing on and off
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'd like to come in about my breathing. It's been going on and off since last summer, I get tight in my chest and kind of short of breath, a lot of the time first thing in the morning and sometimes it wakes me up. My nose has also been stuffy all the time and I sneeze constantly. It's not an emergency I don't think, it just isn't going away.

documents.title: RN triage call back
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Called pt re: portal message. Episodic chest tightness/SOB about 6 months, often early AM, sometimes wakes her. Not short of breath right now, speaking full sentences, no chest pain with exertion, no fever, no leg swelling. Never smoker. Advised ED/911 for severe SOB, chest pain or lips turning blue.
Scheduled with PCP 1/18 at 10:20, 40 min, spirometry setup requested.

events.reason: Shortness of breath, chest tightness, nasal congestion

medications.drug: NDA020983 60 ACTUAT albuterol 0.09 MG/ACTUAT Metered Dose Inhaler
medications.sig: Inhale 1 to 2 puffs by mouth every 4 to 6 hours if needed for wheeze or breathlessness

reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry performed in office. Patient effort good; maneuvers acceptable. Pre-bronchodilator: obstructive pattern, with variability between efforts. Post-bronchodilator (albuterol 4 puffs via spacer, repeat at 15 min): significant improvement in airflow meeting standard reversibility criteria (at least 12% and 200 mL).
reports.conclusion: Variable airflow obstruction with a significant bronchodilator response, consistent with asthma.

documents.title: Office Visit — breathing, nasal symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: chest tightness and shortness of breath on and off for about 6 months.

HPI: 30 y/o F. Since last summer, intermittent episodes of feeling short of breath with tightness across the chest. Most often in the early morning, and some nights it wakes her. Cold air outside and strong smells (cleaning products, perfume) can bring it on. No fever, no sputum, no weight loss. A friend gave her an over-the-counter pill that helps for a few hours and then it comes back; she doesn't know what it was.
Also: nose stuffed up most of the time with a lot of sneezing; she says spring and fall are the worst.
Never smoker. No drugs. Father has asthma.

Meds: sumatriptan 50 mg PRN, HCTZ 25 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 107/71, HR 79, RR 14, T 36.9, SpO2 98% RA. Wt 66.3 kg.
Comfortable, talking in full sentences. Nose: mucosa mildly red and swollen, no polyps. Pharynx clear. Lungs clear, no wheeze even on forced expiration. Heart: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1/S2, no murmur. No edema.

Spirometry today (pre/post albuterol): obstruction that varies effort to effort and improves significantly after bronchodilator, meets reversibility criteria. Report in chart.

A/P
1. Mild persistent asthma — new diagnosis. Night waking and symptoms most days fit persistent, not intermittent. Exam normal between episodes. Reversible obstruction on spirometry.
 - Start montelukast 10 mg nightly as controller. Reviewed the FDA warning: stop it and call if she notices mood changes, unusual dreams or sleep trouble, or anything that feels off psychologically.
 - Albuterol HFA 90 mcg, 1-2 puffs q4-6h PRN. Taught inhaler technique with spacer.
 - Avoid triggers where she can. Asked her not to take the friend's pill anymore.
 - Telehealth check in about 6 weeks.
2. Nasal congestion and sneezing, seasonal worsening — likely allergic rhinitis. Mucosa red and swollen today. Referred to ENT for evaluation. Allergy list unchanged for now.
3. Migraine, HCTZ — no change.

Return sooner or go to the ED for breathlessness not relieved by albuterol.

documents.title: After Visit Summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Today we diagnosed mild persistent asthma.

New medicines:
- Montelukast 10 mg, one tablet every night. This is your daily controller. If you notice changes in mood, sleep or unusual dreams, stop it and message us.
- Albuterol inhaler, 1-2 puffs every 4-6 hours when you're tight or short of breath. Use with the spacer.

Please don't take the pill your friend gave you.

We're sending you to ENT for your nose.

We'll check in by video in about 6 weeks. If albuterol isn't helping or you're struggling to breathe, call 911 or go to the ED.

documents.title: Telehealth — asthma check
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home, identity confirmed.

Six weeks on montelukast. Mornings are a lot better. Woke up with chest tightness once in the last month. Using albuterol maybe twice a week, mostly going out into the cold. No mood or sleep changes on montelukast; she was watching for it.
Nose still congested. ENT appointment set for April.

Appears comfortable on video, no audible wheeze, speaking easily.

A/P: Mild persistent asthma, improving on montelukast. Continue montelukast 10 mg nightly and albuterol PRN. Keep ENT appointment. Recheck at physical in the fall, sooner if albuterol use climbs.

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OTOLARYNGOLOGY — CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of service: 04/13/2022
Referred by: primary care

Reason for referral: chronic nasal congestion and sneezing.

Ms. Williams is a 30 year old woman seen today at the request of her primary care physician, about three months after the visit at which she was diagnosed with mild persistent asthma. Since early spring she has had three weeks of itchy eyes, sneezing and a blocked nose that runs clear. She tells me the same thing happens every year around this time and hangs on until the spring is over. Store-bought antihistamine tablets have done very little.

Medications: albuterol inhaler as needed.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Social: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks per month; graphic designer.

Examination: vital signs within normal limits. Nasal lining pale and boggy with a thin clear drip bilaterally. No tenderness over the maxillary or frontal sinuses. Oropharynx clear. Lungs clear to auscultation.

Impression: Seasonal allergic rhinitis. The timing, recurring each early spring, points to tree and grass pollens. I have added seasonal tree and grass pollen allergy to her record. Formal allergy testing was not performed today.

Plan: She will continue an over-the-counter oral antihistamine through the season. No new prescription today. Return to clinic as needed.

Thank you for allowing me to see her.

Otolaryngology

documents.title: ENT letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Fatou, I got the ENT letter. They think this is seasonal allergies to tree and grass pollen, which fits the every-spring pattern, and I've added that to your allergy list. Their plan is to keep going with an over-the-counter antihistamine for the season. Keep the montelukast going every night for the asthma. Let me know if the spring makes your breathing worse.

documents.title: RE: ENT letter reviewed
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thanks. Breathing has been fine, I only used the inhaler once this week.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
YEARLY PHYSICAL
31 y/o F.

Interval: ENT saw her in April, seasonal allergic rhinitis to tree/grass pollen. Spring was rough for the nose but the OTC antihistamine got her through it.

Asthma: on montelukast nightly. Albuterol roughly once a week or less, more with cold mornings. No night waking since the spring. No ED visits, no steroids. Doing much better than January.

Migraine: sumatriptan two or three times a month, works every time.
Mood good. PHQ-9 = 1.
No other concerns.

Meds: montelukast 10 mg nightly; albuterol HFA PRN; sumatriptan 50 mg PRN (max 200/day); HCTZ 25 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA. Seasonal tree and grass pollens.
Social: unchanged. Never smoker, alcohol rare.

Exam: BP 110/67, HR 82, RR 15, T 36.9, SpO2 98%. Wt 66.1 kg.
Well. HEENT normal, nasal mucosa unremarkable today. Neck: no nodes, thyroid normal. Lungs clear, good air movement. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen benign. Skin: mild comedonal acne on the chin. Ext: no edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. Health maintenance — BMP today (on HCTZ). Flu vaccine and the bivalent COVID booster today. Cervical screening due next year.
2. Mild persistent asthma — reasonably controlled on montelukast. Continue. Albuterol refill sent.
3. Seasonal allergic rhinitis — OTC antihistamine in season.
4. Migraine without aura — stable on PRN sumatriptan.
5. Acne — mild, she's not interested in treatment.
6. HCTZ 25 mg daily — continue.

RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.
